answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when an audited task reveals collusion or fabricated work. Auditors are selected after commitments are locked, and payment depends on verifiable outputs, so creating many names does not multiply rewards. A small anchor deposit can be pictured as a marble at the edge of a lagoon: each identity must put value at risk. A sybil attacker must lock up more capital for each identity and may lose it, making mass identities costly rather than free.
